farground.idle_no_lod: Farground is idle: install Voxy or Distant Horizons to see the distant terrain it generates.

farground.cmd.autotune_cancel: Speed tune cancelled. It won't start on its own again.

farground.reason.waiting_nearby: waiting for the chunks around you to load

farground.reason.done: done - everything in range is generated

farground.tune.waiting_away: speed tune waiting (runs while you are away)
farground.tune.paused: speed tune paused (you moved); it continues when you stand still
farground.tune.start: Tuning speed for this PC (about 1.5 minutes). It stops if you move and picks up again later.
farground.tune.done: Speed tuned: %s chunks at once (about %s chunks/s on this PC).

farground.config.title: Farground
farground.config.distance.intro: How much distant terrain to fill in for Voxy or Distant Horizons. Hover over any setting to see what it does and how much it costs.
farground.config.speed.intro: Farground speeds up while you stand still and backs off while you move, when FPS drops or stutters, and when the game falls behind.
farground.config.enabled.tooltip: Fills in distant terrain in the background.
farground.config.enabled.why.on: Only while there is terrain left to generate.
farground.config.auto_radius: Match my LOD mod's render distance
farground.config.auto_radius.tooltip:
Generates exactly as far as Voxy or Distant Horizons draws,
read from their settings (the larger one if you have both).
Turn off to pick the distance yourself with the slider below.
farground.config.auto_radius.why: Never generates land that can't be seen.
farground.config.radius.tooltip:
How far around you to generate, in chunks (1 chunk = 16 blocks).
Used when "Match my LOD mod's render distance" is off.
farground.config.radius.why: Bigger = longer first fill and more disk space. Once done, it costs nothing.
farground.config.auto_full_detail.toolti:
Works out where Voxy's blocks get too big to show trees,
from Voxy's detail setting, your screen size and FOV.
With only Distant Horizons it uses the slider below (%s chunks by default).
Turn off to pick the distance yourself.
farground.config.auto_full_detail.why: Skips trees nobody could see anyway, so it saves work.
farground.config.full_detail.tooltip:
Trees, ores, caves and structures out to this distance.
Beyond it only the land shape is generated, which looks
the same from far away. Used when Automatic is off.
farground.config.full_detail.why: Full detail chunks take about 3x longer than land shape only.
farground.config.auto_voxel: Auto: no trees past Voxy block size
farground.config.auto_voxel.tooltip:
For Automatic with Voxy: once Voxy draws blocks this big,
trees stop being generated (they can't be seen anyway).
farground.config.auto_voxel.why: Smaller = full detail much further out.
farground.config.other_dim: Full detail in Nether and End (chunks)
farground.config.other_dim.tooltip:
Full detail distance in the Nether and the End.
The Nether ceiling and the End void hide most distant
detail, so a short distance is enough there.
farground.config.gen_overworld.tooltip:
Fill in distant terrain in the Overworld.
Also covers modded dimensions.
farground.config.gen_nether.tooltip: Fill in distant terrain in the Nether.
farground.config.gen_end.tooltip: Fill in distant terrain in the End.
farground.config.gen.why: While there is terrain left to fill in.
farground.config.pause_dh.tooltip:
Only matters if Distant Horizons is installed.
Farground does the generating while it runs; DH just draws.
Not saved to DH's own settings: DH gets its setting back
when Farground is off or the world closes.
farground.config.pause_dh.why.on: Only Farground generates, with its smooth-play limits.
farground.config.pause_dh.why.off: Both generate at once: the same land twice, and more lag.
farground.config.fast_lighting.tooltip:
Works out sky light from the terrain height instead of
Minecraft's lighting pass. Looks the same from far away.
farground.config.fast_lighting.why.on: Skips Minecraft's lighting pass for distant chunks.
farground.config.fast_lighting.why.off: Runs Minecraft's full lighting pass on every chunk.
farground.config.max_concurrent.tooltip:
Most chunks generating at the same time while you stand still.
The speed tune picks a good value for your PC.
farground.config.max_concurrent.why: Higher = faster, but more CPU use.
farground.config.moving.tooltip:
Most chunks generating at once while you walk, fly
or look around. 0 pauses generation while you move.
farground.config.moving.why: This is what you feel while playing: keep it low for smooth movement.
farground.config.idle.tooltip: How long you must stand still before it speeds up.
farground.config.idle.why: Very short waits can cause a hitch when you start moving again.
farground.config.ramp.tooltip:
How many more chunks at once it allows each second
after you stop moving, until it reaches full speed.
farground.config.ramp.why: Faster ramp-up can cause a short hitch when it kicks in.
farground.config.frame_aware: Back off when FPS drops or stutters
farground.config.frame_aware.tooltip:
Slows down when your frame rate dips or you get hitches
(slow 1%% low frames), then speeds back up once it's smooth.
farground.config.frame_aware.why.off: Generation can take frames away from the game.
farground.config.tick_budget: Back off when a game tick takes over
farground.config.tick_budget.tooltip:
Slows down when a game tick takes longer than this.
A tick should take under 50 ms (20 ticks per second).
farground.config.tick_budget.why: Above 50 ms the game itself starts to lag (mobs, crops, redstone).
farground.config.turbo.tooltip:
Runs up to 50%% faster when the game window is in the
background or you haven't moved for a while.
farground.config.turbo.why: Only while you are away, so you won't feel it.
farground.config.away_after.tooltip:
How long without moving before you count as away
(for turbo and the speed tune).
farground.config.away_after.why: Short times can start turbo while you're just looking around.
farground.config.tune_first: Tune speed the first time you're away
farground.config.tune_first.tooltip: Tries a few speeds and keeps the best one for your PC.
farground.config.tune.why: For about 1.5 minutes, once, while you are away.
farground.config.tune_again: Tune again next time I'm away
farground.config.tune_again.tooltip:
Runs the speed tune again. Use after changing mods
or hardware. Same as /farground autotune.
farground.config.memory.tooltip:
Waits while Java memory is still this full right after
a cleanup (a real shortage, not normal use).
farground.config.memory.why.on: Protects against freezes when memory runs low.
farground.config.memory.why.off: Can push the game into long freezes when memory runs out.
farground.config.battery.tooltip: Stops generating while a laptop is unplugged.
farground.config.battery.why.off: Uses battery and makes the laptop warmer.
farground.config.fly_ahead.tooltip:
When flying fast, generates ahead of where you're
heading instead of around where you are.
farground.config.save_unvisited.tooltip:
Keep generated chunks you have never been near.
Off: they're re-created if you go there, and trees or
structures right at the edge of explored land can be cut off.
farground.config.save_unvisited.why.on: Uses more disk space (a few GB at 256 chunks).
farground.config.prune: Free disk space on world close
farground.config.prune.tooltip:
When the world closes, deletes saved chunks you were
never near. Your LOD mod keeps the far view. Changed files are
backed up first. Same as /farground prune. Runs once.
farground.config.prune.why: Closing the world takes a few seconds longer, once.
farground.config.hud.tooltip: A small progress line in a corner of the screen.
farground.config.corner.tooltip: Which corner the progress line sits in.
farground.config.announce.tooltip:
Says in chat when everything in range is generated.
Once per dimension each time you open the world.
